concepts.name: Kitchen hygiene and food safety
concepts.summary: Explain and follow handwashing, separating raw and cooked foods, safe storage temperatures and safe internal cooking temperatures to prevent illness.

concepts.name: Basic knife grip and safety
concepts.summary: Hold a chef's knife with a pinch grip, guide food with a claw hand, and keep the board stable and the blade sharp and safely handled.

concepts.name: Core kitchen tools and measures
concepts.summary: Name common pans, knives, utensils and measuring tools and recall standard units such as teaspoons, tablespoons, cups and grams.

concepts.name: Mise en place
concepts.summary: Understand why reading the whole recipe and prepping and measuring ingredients before heating anything makes cooking calmer and more reliable.

concepts.name: Stovetop heat levels
concepts.summary: Describe what low, medium and high heat look and sound like and how pan and burner settings change how food cooks.

concepts.name: Salt and tasting
concepts.summary: Understand that salt enhances flavour and that tasting during cooking guides seasoning adjustments.

concepts.name: Boiling and simmering
concepts.summary: Tell a rolling boil from a simmer and explain how each is used to cook foods like pasta, rice and eggs.

misconceptions.text: Washing raw chicken before cooking makes it safe to eat.
A dull knife is safer than a sharp one because it cuts less.
Higher heat always cooks food faster and better.

concepts.name: Basic knife cuts
concepts.summary: Produce slices, dices and chopped pieces of consistent size so that ingredients cook evenly.

concepts.name: Roasting vegetables and meats
concepts.summary: Set oven temperature, use a suitable tray and cut size, and judge doneness for roasted vegetables and simple meats.

concepts.name: Following a recipe accurately
concepts.summary: Carry out recipe steps in order using correct quantities, timings and cues such as colour and texture.

concepts.name: Cooking pasta rice and grains
concepts.summary: Cook pasta, rice and grains with suitable water ratios and times to a good texture.

concepts.name: Doneness checks and thermometer use
concepts.summary: Use a thermometer and visual or touch cues to confirm food is cooked safely and to the desired level.

concepts.name: Basic pantry and fat choices
concepts.summary: Choose appropriate oils, butter, acids and staples for different tasks and keep a workable pantry.

concepts.name: Sautéing and pan-frying
concepts.summary: Preheat a pan, add fat, avoid overcrowding and move food appropriately to brown and cook it through.

misconceptions.text: Piling all the food into the pan at once saves time without affecting results.
Meat is done when the outside is browned.
Pieces of any size cook in the same time if the heat is the same.

concepts.name: Maillard browning and caramelisation
concepts.summary: Analyse how dry surfaces, heat and time create browned flavour and adjust technique to achieve or avoid it.

concepts.name: Balancing flavour
concepts.summary: Diagnose a dish as lacking salt, acidity, sweetness, bitterness or richness and correct it with targeted additions.

concepts.name: Moist-heat methods
concepts.summary: Choose and carry out braising, poaching and steaming according to the food's structure and desired result.

concepts.name: Pan sauces and emulsions
concepts.summary: Build a pan sauce by deglazing and reducing, and make a stable vinaigrette or simple emulsion.

concepts.name: Recipe substitution and scaling
concepts.summary: Analyse a recipe's functional ingredients to swap items and scale quantities and cooking times sensibly.

concepts.name: Timing a multi-dish meal
concepts.summary: Plan prep and cooking order so several dishes finish together and hot food is served hot.

concepts.name: Resting and carryover cooking
concepts.summary: Explain how residual heat keeps cooking food and juices redistribute, and pull food early accordingly.

concepts.name: Balanced everyday meal planning
concepts.summary: Compose meals with vegetables, protein and carbohydrate and plan shopping and leftovers across a week.

misconceptions.text: Searing meat seals in the juices.
Wet food browns just as well as dry food if the pan is hot enough.
Any ingredient can be swapped one-for-one in baking and sauces with no effect.

concepts.name: Diagnosing and fixing failed dishes
concepts.summary: Trace a flawed result such as toughness, blandness or a split sauce to its cause and choose a corrective step.

concepts.name: Selecting method by ingredient structure
concepts.summary: Judge the best cooking method for a cut or vegetable based on its connective tissue, fat, moisture and thickness.

concepts.name: Intuitive heat management
concepts.summary: Read sound, smell and visual cues to adjust heat, pan choice and oven position during cooking.

concepts.name: Layering flavour through the cook
concepts.summary: Decide when to add aromatics, salt, spices and acid to build depth and judge the effect of each stage.

concepts.name: Building dishes from principles
concepts.summary: Evaluate available ingredients and apply flexible templates such as stir-fries, soups and roasts to improvise a coherent dish.

concepts.name: Efficient kitchen workflow
concepts.summary: Analyse workflow, batch prep and storage to cut waste and time while keeping food safe and fresh.

concepts.name: Evaluating recipe quality
concepts.summary: Assess whether a recipe's ratios, times and instructions are sound before cooking it and justify changes.

misconceptions.text: Great cooks never need to measure or follow ratios.
A published recipe is always tested and correct as written.
All tough cuts of meat just need more time at high heat to become tender.

concepts.name: Designing original dishes
concepts.summary: Create a new dish with coherent flavour, texture and balance and refine it through iterative testing.

concepts.name: Writing reliable recipes
concepts.summary: Produce clear, tested recipes with accurate quantities, cues and troubleshooting that others can reproduce.

concepts.name: Cross-cuisine technique adaptation
concepts.summary: Evaluate techniques and flavour systems from different cuisines and adapt them respectfully to new ingredients.

concepts.name: Menu design for diets and constraints
concepts.summary: Design menus that meet allergy, dietary, budget and seasonal constraints without losing flavour or nutritional balance.

concepts.name: Evidence-based technique evaluation
concepts.summary: Judge cooking claims and techniques using food science and controlled comparison rather than tradition alone.

concepts.name: Teaching and coaching cooks
concepts.summary: Create lessons and feedback that diagnose a learner's gaps and build their skill and confidence.

concepts.name: Sustainable and economical kitchen systems
concepts.summary: Design routines for sourcing, using whole ingredients and repurposing leftovers to reduce cost and waste.

misconceptions.text: Authentic technique means never adapting a dish to different ingredients or needs.
Traditional kitchen rules are proven and need no testing.
A new dish is finished once it tastes good once.
